pr_title: Fix handling of vector instruction sets in NativeAOT compiler
pr_body:
The virtual vector instruction used internally by the JIT were leaking out and reported as unsupported

Fixes #68222
pr_comments: Would it be possible to add a regression test for this to tests\nativeaot\SmokeTests\HardwareIntrinsics? The ISA handling is all quite confusing and that test is the only thing that gives me reasonable assurance it's all working in the end result.
The test would have to have multiple versions of hardcoded asm code for a method that does `Vector<T>` operation, like comparing two vectors. Is it what you had in mind?

> The test would have to have multiple versions of hardcoded asm code for a method that does `Vector<T>` operation, like comparing two vectors. Is it what you had in mind?

Hm, maybe not worth it if that's the case. I was hoping there would be something else that is observable. Maybe perf testing will be a good enough regression test.
Superpmi replay errors are known issue: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/68196#issuecomment-1103263507

> I was hoping there would be something else that is observable

I do not see anything easily observable. 

In theory, the problem would be observable by `Vector128/256.IsHardwareAccelerated`. Unfortunately, the mapping of the vector ISA to physical ISA is done on the JIT side for these APIs: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c49904522e3410350a7f27cbee18707b6171ed1d/src/coreclr/jit/hwintrinsic.cpp#L290-L304 .
